body.statement:
For every fixed \(K\ge2\), \(q\in\mathbb R^K\), and positive \(R_g,R_e\), over the balanced finite and stationary pairwise-orthogonal classes,
\[
\lim_{T\to\infty}V_{T,K}(q;R_g,R_e)
=V_{\infty,K}(q;R_g,R_e)
=R_e^2N_q^2.
\]
The finite and stationary infima are unchanged if one restricts to globally sign-symmetric laws.  For every power of two \(L\ge2d\), \(D_L^{\mathrm G}\in\mathfrak D_{\infty}\), it is globally sign symmetric, it has a hidden-state implementation with at most \(2L^2\) states, and
\[
\mathcal R_{\infty,K}(D_L^{\mathrm G})
=\max\!\left\{R_e^2N_q^2,\frac{R_g^2}{L}\lambda_{\max}\!\bigl(D_q(M_L+H_d)D_q^{\top}\bigr)\right\}.
\]
Consequently, if \(L\ge\max\{2d,B_KR_g^2/R_e^2\}\), then \(\mathcal R_{\infty,K}(D_L^{\mathrm G})=R_e^2N_q^2\).
body.proof_tex:
We first verify feasibility and implementation.  The independent uniform phase in the Golay-block definition makes \(D_L^{\mathrm G}\) invariant under every integer shift.  The one- and two-point identities in the tensor-certificate lemma give
\[
\mathbb E[X_t^{\infty}]=0,
\qquad
\mathbb E[X_s^{\infty}X_t^{\infty}]=0\quad(s\ne t).
\]
Thus \(D_L^{\mathrm G}\in\mathfrak D_{\infty}\) under the enlarged stationary definition.  Replacing every independent block sign \(\sigma\) by \(-\sigma\) globally negates the emitted path without changing the joint law, so this particular design is globally sign symmetric.

Write \(L=2^p\).  A hidden state can be taken as
\[
(r,\alpha,\sigma)\in\{0,\ldots,L-1\}\times\mathbb F_2^p\times\{-1,+1\}.
\]
There are \(L\cdot L\cdot2=2L^2\) such states.  For \(r<L-1\), advance \(r\) deterministically and retain \((\alpha,\sigma)\); at \(r=L-1\), reset \(r\) to zero and draw a fresh independent uniform pair \((\alpha,\sigma)\).  The uniform distribution on the state set is invariant, and its emission is exactly the random-phase independent-block law.  This proves the finite-state claim.

Fix such an \(L\).  The zero-prehistory lemma and the lag-sum covariance limit in the tensor-certificate lemma yield
\[
T\mathbb E[u_Tu_T^{\top}]
\longrightarrow \frac1L D_q(M_L+H_d)D_q^{\top},
\tag{24}
\]
because the uniformly bounded remainder contributes \(o(1)\) after the displayed normalization, including its covariance with the leading term.  The same zero-prehistory lemma gives
\[
T^2\lVert F_{T,q}\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}^2\longrightarrow N_q^2.
\tag{25}
\]
Every finite restriction of \(D_L^{\mathrm G}\) is balanced and pairwise orthogonal.  Its global sign symmetry, together with the evenness of \(u_T\) and oddness of \(v_T\), makes \(\mathbb E[u_Tv_T^{\top}]=0\).  The exact-risk lemma, (24), (25), and continuity of the largest eigenvalue therefore give
\[
\mathcal R_{\infty,K}(D_L^{\mathrm G})
=\max\!\left\{R_e^2N_q^2,\frac{R_g^2}{L}\lambda_{\max}\!\bigl(D_q(M_L+H_d)D_q^{\top}\bigr)\right\}.
\tag{26}
\]

We next certify the stated sufficient block length.  For \(1\le h< L/2\), the tensor-certificate lemma gives \(\lvert C_{L,h}(W)\rvert\le h\).  If \(L=2d\) and \(h=d=L/2\), the same bound follows directly because \(C_{L,h}\) is a sum of exactly \(L-h=h\) signs.  Consequently, for every \(L\ge2d\),
\[
\operatorname{tr}(M_L+H_d)
=\sum_{h=1}^{d}\{\mathbb E[C_{L,h}(W)^2]+h\}
\le\sum_{h=1}^{d}(h^2+h).
\tag{27}
\]
From the definition of \(D_q\), each entry is a sum of at most two shifted coefficients.  Applying \((a+b)^2\le2a^2+2b^2\) entrywise and counting, for each \(q_j\), the \(d-j\) lower shifts and the \(j\) upper shifts gives
\[
\lVert D_q\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}^2
\le\lVert D_q\rVert_{\mathrm F}^2
\le2\sum_{j=0}^{d}\{(d-j)+j\}q_j^2
=2d\lVert q\rVert_2^2.
\tag{28}
\]
Direct integration of the finite polynomial and orthogonality of the exponentials give
\[
\lVert q\rVert_2^2
=\frac1{2\pi}\int_0^{2\pi}\lvert Q_q(e^{i\omega})\rvert^2\,d\omega
\le N_q^2.
\tag{29}
\]
Since \(M_L+H_d\) is positive semidefinite, (27)--(29) imply
\[
\begin{aligned}
\lambda_{\max}\!\bigl(D_q(M_L+H_d)D_q^{\top}\bigr)
&\le\lVert D_q\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}^2\operatorname{tr}(M_L+H_d)\\
&\le2dN_q^2\sum_{h=1}^{d}(h^2+h)
=B_KN_q^2.
\end{aligned}
\tag{30}
\]
If \(L\ge B_KR_g^2/R_e^2\), division is legitimate because \(R_e>0\), and (30) makes the signal term in (26) at most \(R_e^2N_q^2\).  Hence the displayed disturbance floor is attained.  If \(q=0\), both sides are zero and the same conclusion holds.

It remains to prove global optimality and equality of the two limits.  For any balanced pairwise-orthogonal finite law, the noise matrix is a principal block of the unsymmetrized risk matrix in the exact-risk lemma.  The Rayleigh-quotient argument therefore gives the design-independent lower bound
\[
\mathcal R_T(D)\ge T^2R_e^2\lVert F_{T,q}\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}^2.
\tag{31}
\]
Taking the finite-design infimum and using (25) yields
\[
\liminf_{T\to\infty}V_{T,K}(q;R_g,R_e)\ge R_e^2N_q^2.
\tag{32}
\]
Choose one power of two \(L\) satisfying the two lower bounds in the theorem.  Its restriction is feasible for every \(T\), so
\[
V_{T,K}(q;R_g,R_e)\le\mathcal R_T(D_L^{\mathrm G}|_{1:T}).
\]
Equations (24)--(26) and (30) make the right side converge to \(R_e^2N_q^2\).  Combined with (32), this proves
\[
\lim_{T\to\infty}V_{T,K}(q;R_g,R_e)=R_e^2N_q^2.
\tag{33}
\]
For any \(P_{\infty}\in\mathfrak D_{\infty}\), every finite restriction is in \(\mathfrak D_T\), so (31) and (25) imply
\[
\mathcal R_{\infty,K}(P_{\infty})\ge R_e^2N_q^2.
\]
The chosen Golay law attains equality by (26) and (30).  Taking the stationary infimum proves
\[
V_{\infty,K}(q;R_g,R_e)=R_e^2N_q^2,
\]
which together with (33) proves the asserted limit equality.

Finally, for an arbitrary \(P_{\infty}\in\mathfrak D_{\infty}\), define its global-sign average by \(P_{\infty}^{\pm}(B)=\{P_{\infty}(B)+P_{\infty}(-B)\}/2\).  Reflection and mixing preserve stationarity, balance, and zero autocorrelation.  Each finite restriction is the sign symmetrization of the corresponding restriction of \(P_{\infty}\), so the exact-risk lemma gives
\[
\mathcal R_T(P_{\infty}^{\pm}|_{1:T})
\le\mathcal R_T(P_{\infty}|_{1:T})
\quad\text{for every }T.
\]
Taking upper limits shows \(\mathcal R_{\infty,K}(P_{\infty}^{\pm})\le\mathcal R_{\infty,K}(P_{\infty})\).  The identical finite-law conclusion is already part of the exact-risk lemma.  Since globally sign-symmetric laws form a subclass but every legal law has a no-worse symmetrized representative, both infima are unchanged by imposing that representative property.
body.justification: The theorem identifies the stationary efficiency frontier over the enlarged balanced class and supplies a finite-state optimizer with a matching spectral lower bound.
body.gap: Complementary deterministic inputs and iid analyses do not prove one-path design-based minimax MSE, the finite-state randomized law, or equality with the finite-horizon limit over all balanced pairwise-orthogonal designs.
body.consumer: It gives an implementable long-horizon binary randomization for individualized impulse-response experiments while allowing treatment counts to remain random.
